# Temple Scroll Column 54 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 54 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 54:1 — "lend-at-interest" vs. "charge interest" vs. "charge interest"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lend-at-interest" | Literal tashikh — verbal form preserving Hebrew morphology |
| LOGOS | "charge interest" | Standard English financial/legal term |
| PNEUMA | "charge interest" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "charge interest" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The English idiom is clear and precise; EMET's hyphenated compound is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 54:8 — "document of cutting-off" vs. "certificate of divorce" vs. "letter of divorce"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "document of cutting-off" | Literal sefer keritut — preserving the root k-r-t ("to cut") |
| LOGOS | "certificate of divorce" | Standard legal and biblical translation term |
| PNEUMA | "letter of divorce" | Accessible modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "certificate of divorce" (LOGOS). This is the universally recognized rendering in English biblical and legal scholarship.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 54:8 — "thing of nakedness" vs. "something indecent" vs. "something objectionable"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "thing of nakedness" | Literal ervat davar — preserving the Hebrew legal phrase |
| LOGOS | "something indecent" | Captures the impropriety without the anatomical overtone |
| PNEUMA | "something objectionable" | Broader modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "something indecent" (LOGOS). EMET's "thing of nakedness" is confusing in English; PNEUMA's "objectionable" is too generic and loses the specific connotation of moral/physical impropriety.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 54:13 — "taking-as-a-pledge a soul" vs. "taking a life as a pledge" vs. "taking away his means of survival"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "taking-as-a-pledge a soul" | Literal nefesh — "soul/life" preserved |
| LOGOS | "taking a life as a pledge" | Translates nefesh as "life" — the person depends on the millstone for sustenance |
| PNEUMA | "taking away his means of survival" | Interpretive rendering explaining why the millstone pledge is prohibited |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "taking a life as a pledge" (LOGOS). EMET's "soul" sounds theological rather than practical; PNEUMA's paraphrase, while insightful, is interpretation rather than translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 54:14 — "stealing a soul" vs. "kidnapping" vs. "kidnapping"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stealing a soul from among his brothers" | Literal gonev nefesh — "stealing a soul/person" |
| LOGOS | "kidnapping one of his brothers" | English legal equivalent of the Hebrew |
| PNEUMA | "kidnapping a fellow Israelite" | Same concept, modernized phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "kidnapping" (LOGOS). The Hebrew "stealing a soul" refers specifically to abduction of persons; "kidnapping" is the precise English legal term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 54:15 — "skin-disease" vs. "skin disease" vs. "infectious skin disease"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "skin-disease" | Tsara'at rendered as compound |
| LOGOS | "skin disease" | Same without hyphenation |
| PNEUMA | "infectious skin disease" | Adds "infectious" to explain the quarantine context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "skin disease" (LOGOS). All three agree on rejecting "leprosy." PNEUMA's "infectious" adds medical interpretation not present in the text; tsara'at may include non-infectious conditions.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
